newsitem.title: USA: UN Sec-General to offer Iraq oil report next week.
newsitem.headline: UN Sec-General to offer Iraq oil report next week.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan will offer the Security Council his recommendations on Iraq oil-for-food accord renewal early next week, a U.N. spokesman said Tuesday.
Details of the report were being finalized this week and no conclusions were being drawn on whether the secretary-general would recommend renewal, U.N. spokesman Yasuhiro Ueki said.
"The report will be sumbitted at the beginning of next week, it will be a very comprehensive report," Ueki said.
However, high-ranking U.N. officials said last week that the secretary-general would certainly favor a six-month renewal of the $2 billion accord at current oil sales limits.

The final decision on renewal of the plan is up to the 15-member Security Council. Possible American roadblocks appeared last week when U.S. Ambassador Bill Richardson said Washington was not convinced the accord was implemented as intended.
Once Annan's report is submitted, the Security Council is expected to act on the matter sometime before the end of next week.
Western diplomats said they hoped council action on renewal would occur before the current plan expires on June 7, less than two weeks from today.

The oil accord went into effect on December 10, allowing Baghdad to export oil for 180 days, mainly to buy food and supplies as a humanitarian exception to U.N. sanctions slapped on Iraq after the 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
